headline: BLOWOUT NFP HAMMERS GOLD — 162K Payrolls vs 56K Forecast Revives September Rate-Hike Bets; XAU/USD Breaks Below $4,400
snippet: August nonfarm payrolls blew past forecasts at 162,000 — nearly triple the 56,000 consensus — sending gold down more than 2% and briefly below $4,400 as Fed rate-hike probability surged back toward 60%. The print effectively wiped out the dovish signal from Governor Waller's Thursday remarks, pushing the September 15-16 FOMC meeting back to a live hike decision and putting $4,300 support back in play for bullion.

headline: CHINA PULLS LICENCE FROM WORLD'S LARGEST LITHIUM MINE — CATL Jianxiawo Back On Care & Maintenance; Benchmark MI Slashes Supply Forecast 49%
snippet: Chinese regulators revoked the environmental approval for CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Sichuan — China's largest lithium mine by installed capacity — forcing an indefinite return to care and maintenance. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence immediately cut its 2026 Chinese mined lithium output forecast by 49%, from 62,500 to 32,000 tonnes LCE, compounding a structural supply squeeze in a market already up 102% year-on-year.

headline: KENORLAND HITS GOLD IN 8 OF 9 HOLES AT WESTERN WABIGOON — Maiden 4,089m Drill Program Confirms Shear-Hosted Hydrothermal System; TSX-V: KLD
snippet: Kenorland Minerals (TSX-V: KLD) reported gold mineralization in eight of nine drill holes from its maiden 4,089-metre diamond program at the W2 target of the Western Wabigoon Project in northwestern Ontario, confirming a shear-hosted gold-bearing hydrothermal system over meaningful width. The results establish Western Wabigoon as a drill-ready resource target in a corridor that hosts several past-producing and advanced-stage gold mines.

headline: ASIAN METALS WRAP SEPT. 4: GOLD UNDER PRESSURE, PLATINUM STEADY, BASE METALS MIXED AHEAD OF NFP
snippet: GoldSeek's September 4 Asian metals market update covers price action across gold, silver, platinum group metals, and base metals during the Asian session ahead of the US nonfarm payrolls release, with gold consolidating below $4,500 and base metals mixed on thin pre-report volume. The briefing tracks London AM fix references and Shanghai futures as the dollar holds steady ahead of the decisive US data print.

headline: GREENLAND MINES CLOSES $35M SARFARTOQ Nd-Pr DEAL — Southwest Greenland REE Project Secured; Neo Performance Materials Takes 60% Offtake; NASDAQ: GRML
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd. (NASDAQ: GRML) completed its acquisition of Neo North Star Resources on September 1, securing the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earth project in southwest Greenland for $20 million cash and $15 million in securities. Neo Performance Materials became a strategic shareholder with offtake rights for up to 60% of future Sarfartoq production, establishing a direct mine-to-magnet NdPr supply chain outside Chinese control.

headline: NT1 SIGNS $500M SPAC MERGER WITH PLUTONIAN II — Australian Explorer Targets NYSE Listing; Completion Expected 2027
snippet: Australian mineral exploration company NT1 agreed to merge with Plutonian Acquisition Corp. II at an enterprise value of $500 million (A$694 million), targeting a New York Stock Exchange listing once regulatory approvals are secured, with completion anticipated in 2027. The deal continues a trend of resource juniors accessing deep US capital pools via SPAC structures rather than a traditional ASX or TSX-V float.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE SURGE RESCUES LITHIUM DEMAND — Grid Battery Boom Offsets EV Slowdown; Bald Hill And Finniss Restart Into Higher Price
snippet: Stationary grid-scale battery storage has emerged as the unexpected demand floor for lithium in 2026, absorbing volumes that bearish EV forecasts predicted would keep prices suppressed. Lithium carbonate prices have risen more than 102% year-on-year, and Australian producers are responding: Mineral Resources restarted its Bald Hill hard-rock lithium mine after an 18-month suspension, while Core Lithium brought the Finniss project back online, adding new western supply.

headline: SILVER'S UNSUNG STRENGTH: 116% ABOVE YEAR-AGO LEVEL — China's Strategic Reclassification And Industrial Demand Are Powering A Quiet Bull Market
snippet: Silver is averaging nearly $74/oz in 2026 — 116.7% above the comparable 2025 period — yet remains systematically underplayed relative to gold's record-setting coverage, according to a GoldSeek analysis. The piece argues that China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material, a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, and rising industrial demand from solar and electronics manufacturing have created a structural setup retail investors are underweighting.

headline: PALADIN ENERGY DRILLS NEW HIGH-GRADE URANIUM AT PATTERSON LAKE SOUTH — 2026 Exploration Campaign Extends PLS System; TSX: PDN
snippet: Paladin Energy (TSX: PDN) released high-grade uranium drill results from the Patterson Lake South project in Saskatchewan, extending the known mineralized footprint at one of the highest-grade undeveloped uranium systems in the Athabasca Basin's southwest corridor. The results add exploration upside to Paladin's producing Langer Heinrich asset in Namibia and come as spot uranium holds at $82/lb following an 8% recovery in September.

headline: COPPER STALLS BELOW $14,200 AS GLOBAL GROWTH FEARS RESURFACE — Post-Tariff Front-Loading Fades; Chile July Output Off 9.4%
snippet: Three-month LME copper slipped below $14,200 per tonne after the tariff-driven front-loading surge that briefly set a record close last week began to unwind on renewed global growth concerns. Chile's July copper production fell 9.4% year-on-year as severe weather and planned maintenance weighed on Codelco and Escondida output, adding a structural supply story beneath the near-term demand uncertainty.
